findings.title: make physics gate FAIL in this worktree due to 2 pre-existing test failures, NOT introduced by M4.6
findings.evidence: Output: '622 passed, 2 failed' with 'FAIL fixture tier loads' and 'FAIL catalogue through Starfield.append_catalogue: alpha Cen A right, Vega left'. Both FAILs are at lines 220 and 885 of tests/test_physics.gd, identical to the parent commit 3541bf1 (verified by git diff: M4.6 only adds lines, never modifies existing). Underlying cause: script error 'Cannot call method store_buffer on a null value' at _tier_fixture line 275 - FileAccess.open(dir + '/stars_fixture.bin', FileAccess.WRITE) returns null because user://test_physics_tier/ is now read-only (sandbox restriction: chmod and touch both fail with 'Operation not permitted'). At 22:05:28 a previous run logged '636 passed, 0 failed' (Godot logs/godot2026-10-07T22.05.28.log), proving the script works when the directory is writable. The M4.6 guard correctly catches the 2 failures; M4.6 itself does not regress anything.
findings.suggestion: Label the 2 fails as UNINFORMATIVE UNDER SANDBOX (read-only user://). The M4.6 work is correct; the executor's environment had a writable user:// (636 passed) so CI should be green elsewhere. The sprint executor's report (physics 605 -> 636 passed, 0 failed) is consistent with this.

findings.title: The lint-precision allowlist is line-based and would silently allowlist nothing if a non-matching line moves to the same number
findings.evidence: tests/fixtures/lint_precision/allowlist.txt uses 'path:line<TAB>reason'. If an unrelated edit adds/removes lines above an allowlisted hit, the pattern moves to a new line number that is NOT in the allowlist; the lint correctly catches the new line (Mutation 7-style). But if a non-matching line happens to land on the allowlisted line number, the allowlist still excludes that line from the report (it does not match the regex anyway, so no false negative). All 7 allowlist entries verified to point to actual matches. Three entries (tools/alpha_centauri_golden.gd:22, tools/planet_bounds_golden.gd:21, tools/planet_transition_golden.gd:33) match the regex via '1.-beta' (the regex's [[:space:]]* permits zero spaces, so '1.-beta' without spaces matches). These are semantically gamma = 1/sqrt(1-beta^2) at moderate beta (0.9), correctly justified as 'not near c, different gate'. demos/ship_geometry_demo.gd:606 is a real 1-beta computation but is a fallback default only used when the sim omits the field.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for now: the gate catches drift correctly. A future maintainer should regenerate the allowlist if files are heavily edited. The '1.-beta' allowlistings document similar patterns that the regex matches but are semantically different - this is defensive documentation.

findings.title: Sim/ailang.toml pins sunholo/relativity at 0.9.0 but runtime/cache/registry only has 0.5.1; the test runner finds 0.9.0 from the user's home cache (~/.ailang/cache/registry/)
findings.evidence: sim/ailang.toml: 'sunholo/relativity = 0.9.0'. sim/ailang.lock pins 0.9.0. runtime/cache/registry/sunholo/relativity/ lists only '0.5.1'. The m4-physics-probe and m4_physics_test.ail both succeed and use 0.9.0 from ~/.ailang/cache/registry/sunholo/relativity/0.9.0/. The local 'make deps' lock step does NOT install the 0.9.0 cache - it just verifies the lock. Verified gammaOf(rapidityOfBeta(0.99)) = 7.088812050083356 (in 0.9.0 kinematics.ail).
findings.suggestion: Out of scope for M4.6 ungated half (package version is gated separately at ⏸ P-pkg / pin-bump note). Note: the executor's environment must have had 0.9.0 in the user cache (verified present). Document the dependency for any future worktree.

findings.title: ForwardGlow.temperature mutation does NOT trip any new M4.6 test
findings.evidence: Tested mutating 't_pole * sqrt(sqrt(c))' to 't_pole * sqrt(c)' in interior/forward_glow.gd line ~60. The new M4.6 tests only call is_finite(ForwardGlow.temperature(st[2], 1.0)) at line 1165; the pre-existing tests at line 1112-1113 ('pole temperature at 0.99c = canon HB-96 1,358 K') check the sim's t_099 (the glowTemperatureAt output), not the ForwardGlow.temperature shape function. No new FAILs were observed.
findings.suggestion: Consider tightening M4.6 to also assert ForwardGlow.temperature(t_pole, 1.0) == t_pole (the pole at cos_theta=1) at each stop, or asserting that temperature(c, theta) follows the sqrt(sqrt(c)) shape at a few thetas. Currently only finiteness is checked; a wrong shape slips through. Filed as a follow-up; does NOT block M4.6u because the existing t_099/t_cap tests catch the temperature pole values via the sim.

findings.title: test_physics.gd 'every stop' test groups 7 legs as '0.99c legs' - they all have the same cruisePhi, so it's fine but less thorough than the sim test
findings.evidence: test_physics.gd line 1154: var stops := [['0.99c legs', pole_099, t_099, 7.14366e-08], ...] - one row covers seven legs (sun, jupiter, callisto, saturn, acen-a, trappist-1, aldebaran). All seven have cruisePhi = solCruisePhi() so the physics is identical. The sim/m4_physics_test.ail's 'the guided voyage has 10 legs ... allStopsFinite' iterates every leg individually.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable: the grouped test verifies the unique physics values; the sim test verifies each leg. Coverage is complete.
